title: In '…', use '…' when comparing constant literals not '…' ('…').
summary: Used when comparing an object to a literal, which is usually what you do not want to do, since you can compare to a different literal than what was expected altogether. pylint calls it literal-comparison.
message_templates: In '{}', use '{}' when comparing constant literals not '{}' ('{}')

title: Redundant comparison - ….
summary: Used when something is compared against itself. pylint calls it comparison-with-itself.

title: Comparison between constants: "… … …" has a constant value.
summary: When two literals are compared with each other the result is a constant. Using the constant directly is both easier to read and more performant. Initializing 'True' and 'False' this way is not required since Python 2.3. pylint calls it comparison-of-constants.
message_templates: Comparison between constants: "{} {} {}" has a constant value

title: Consider using a decorator instead of calling classmethod.
summary: Used when a class method is defined without using the decorator syntax. pylint calls it no-classmethod-decorator.
message_templates: Consider using a decorator instead of calling classmethod

title: Consider using a decorator instead of calling staticmethod.
summary: Used when a static method is defined without using the decorator syntax. pylint calls it no-staticmethod-decorator.
message_templates: Consider using a decorator instead of calling staticmethod

title: Class … inherits from object, can be safely removed from bases in python3.
summary: Used when a class inherit from object, which under python3 is implicit, hence can be safely removed from bases. pylint calls it useless-object-inheritance.
message_templates: Class {} inherits from object, can be safely removed from bases in python3

title: Cannot have defined parameters for properties.
summary: Used when we detect that a property also has parameters, which are useless, given that properties cannot be called with additional arguments. pylint calls it property-with-parameters.
message_templates: Cannot have defined parameters for properties

title: Cyclic import (…).
summary: Used when a cyclic import between two or more modules is detected. pylint calls it cyclic-import.

title: Use 'from … import …' instead.
summary: Emitted when a submodule of a package is imported and aliased with the same name, e.g., instead of import concurrent.futures as futures use from concurrent import futures. pylint calls it consider-using-from-import.

title: Similar lines in … files.
summary: Indicates that a set of similar lines has been detected among multiple file. This usually means that the code should be refactored to avoid this duplication. pylint calls it duplicate-code.

title: Too many ancestors (…/…).
summary: Used when class has too many parent classes, try to reduce this to get a simpler (and so easier to use) class. pylint calls it too-many-ancestors.

title: Too many instance attributes (…/…).
summary: Used when class has too many instance attributes, try to reduce this to get a simpler (and so easier to use) class. pylint calls it too-many-instance-attributes.

title: Too few public methods (…/…).
summary: Used when class has too few public methods, so be sure it's really worth it. pylint calls it too-few-public-methods.

title: Too many public methods (…/…).
summary: Used when class has too many public methods, try to reduce this to get a simpler (and so easier to use) class. pylint calls it too-many-public-methods.

title: Too many return statements (…/…).
summary: Used when a function or method has too many return statement, making it hard to follow. pylint calls it too-many-return-statements.

title: Too many branches (…/…).
summary: Used when a function or method has too many branches, making it hard to follow. pylint calls it too-many-branches.

title: Too many arguments (…/…).
summary: Used when a function or method takes too many arguments. pylint calls it too-many-arguments.

title: Too many local variables (…/…).
summary: Used when a function or method has too many local variables. pylint calls it too-many-locals.

title: Too many statements (…/…).
summary: Used when a function or method has too many statements. You should then split it in smaller functions / methods. pylint calls it too-many-statements.

title: Too many boolean expressions in if statement (…/…).
summary: Used when an if statement contains too many boolean expressions. pylint calls it too-many-boolean-expressions.
message_templates: Too many boolean expressions in if statement ({}/{})

title: Too many positional arguments (…/…).
summary: Used when a function has too many positional arguments. pylint calls it too-many-positional-arguments.
